claims.text: The dynamic mechanical behavior of as-cast or wrought CoCrFeMnNi is primarily mediated by formation of a heterogeneous microstructure.
The relevant heterogeneous microstructure contains both FCC and BCC phases.
FCC and BCC phases interact through dislocation glide, twinning, and grain-boundary sliding.
The combined deformation mechanisms enhance both strength and ductility.
The initial material is an as-cast or wrought CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy.
The structural mediator is an FCC+BCC heterogeneous microstructure.
Dislocation glide contributes to the proposed dynamic mechanical response.
Twinning contributes to the proposed dynamic mechanical response.
Grain-boundary sliding contributes to the proposed dynamic mechanical response.
CoCrFeMnNi will have 20% higher yield strength than single-phase FCC NiCoCr.
CoCrFeMnNi will have 30% higher ductility than single-phase FCC NiCoCr.
The proposed mechanism and performance improvements should hold from strain rates of 10^-5 to 10^-1 s^-1 and temperatures of 298 to 773 K.
Failure to exceed the baseline yield strength by at least 15% and baseline ductility by at least 25% would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted increases are 20% in yield strength and 30% in ductility, but the falsification thresholds are only 15% and 25%. Thus, results below the stated predictions could still avoid falsification, leaving an ambiguous interval.
